text:
ryan: Quick proposal — deprecate the session-affinity header and replace it with `X-Redwood-Reflex` (a compact reflexive client-config) to unify routing metadata and sampling. This should stop weird quota attribution when proxies rewrite headers. Thoughts?
anita: what exactly does `X-Redwood-Reflex` carry? route id + sampling only?
ryan: yup — route_hint, a 1-bit sampling flag, and an opt-in telemetry bit. Compact ascii/base64 like `routeId:0x12|s:1|t:0` (we'll formalize).
sam: will this break older SDKs that only emit session-affinity?
ryan: plan is graceful: SDKs (py/ts/go) will be bumped to emit `X-Redwood-Reflex` and also keep session-affinity for a 2-week fallback window. Runtime prefers reflex header if present.
julie: console impact: dashboard aggregation and historical metrics need a mapping layer for the rollout window to avoid gaps. ops-bot: create ticket RED-3145 for dashboard work pls.
ops-bot: Ticket created: RED-3145 — "Reflex header rollout: dashboard mapping + normalizer" (assignee: julie).
sam: how do we avoid double-counting/billing edge cases if proxies forward both headers?
ryan: runtime dedup rule: prefer `X-Redwood-Reflex` when present; if both present, treat as single request and use reflex for attribution. Billing pipeline will dedupe based on request_id + routeKey.
anita: telemetry/privacy: sampling bit is technically data. We should gate it behind SDK opt-in (already supported by client telemetry opt-in). Add explicit config flag in SDKs.
sam: rollout steps?
ryan: proposed timeline: (1) RFC merged today, (2) SDK PRs w/ fallback by EOD Fri, (3) Console mapping + metric normalizer next week, (4) start canaries on Dedicated, (5) remove session-affinity fallback after 14 days.
julie: add a dashboard tile during rollout to show % of requests using reflex vs session-affinity and mismatches. That'll help ops decide when to flip the kill switch.
ryan: agreed. julie — can you drop a quick mock and a list of required metric transforms? link to mock when ready.
julie: will do. putting a figma link: https://figma.com/file/xyz — will add transform spec in RED-3145.
sam: I'll start py/ts PRs. small question: how do we encode legacy route ids that are long? do we hash?
ryan: yes, hash + truncate to 64-bit hex to keep header < 64 chars. Documented in RFC.
sam: ok tagging @anita for telemetry opt-in language in SDK.
anita: will draft consent copy.
ryan: thanks — if no blockers I'll open the RFC and create the SDK issue trackers. :thumbsup:
